method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. claims.claim: **Immediate management aims to minimise ongoing neurological damage** while investigation and treatment are started.
claims.source_text: The aim of immediate management is to minimise ongoing neurological damage while investigation and treatment are initiated
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Parents are the best judge of an altered conscious state**, particularly for children with disability. Take parental and nursing concerns seriously.
claims.source_text: Parents are the best judge of an altered conscious state, particularly for children with disability … Parental and nursing concerns of conscious state should be taken seriously
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider child abuse** in a young child presenting with altered conscious state and signs of injury.
claims.source_text: Consider child abuse in a young child presenting with altered conscious state and signs of injury
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Altered conscious state is defined by a GCS below 15.** It is uncommon but carries significant mortality and morbidity; **head injury and infection are the most common causes of paediatric coma.**
claims.source_text: altered conscious state defined by a GCS of < 15 … Altered conscious state is an uncommon presentation but is associated with significant mortality and morbidity … Head injury and infection are the most common causes of paediatric coma
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Screen with AVPU** (Alert, responds to Voice, responds to Pain, Unresponsive), particularly in younger children. **Any impairment on AVPU → formal GCS.**
claims.source_text: Initial screening of conscious state may be done using AVPU scale, particularly in younger children … A = Alert V = Responds to voice P = Responds to pain U = Unresponsive … Any impairment on AVPU scale should prompt a formal assessment of GCS
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Trauma and infection:** head injury, falls, concussion; meningitis, encephalitis, sepsis, cerebral and extracerebral abscesses, malaria.
claims.source_text: Trauma Blunt, penetrating head injury, falls, concussion … Infection Meningitis, encephalitis, sepsis, cerebral and extracerebral abscesses, malaria
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Neurological:** post-ictal phase or status epilepticus; raised intracranial pressure (mass, cerebral oedema, **blocked VP shunt**); cerebral hypoxia or ischaemia from respiratory failure, shock, asphyxiation or stroke/intracranial haemorrhage.
claims.source_text: Epilepsy: Post-ictal phase, status epilepticus … Raised intracranial pressure: Mass lesion, cerebral oedema, blocked ventriculoperitoneal shunt … Cerebral hypoxia, ischaemia: Respiratory failure, shock (cardiogenic, adrenal crisis, sepsis, hypovolaemia), asphyxiation, cerebrovascular event (stroke/intracranial haemorrhage)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Poisoning and metabolic:** alcohol, hallucinogens, opiates, lead; **hypoglycaemia**, DKA, renal or hepatic failure, hypo/hypernatraemia, hypothermia, inborn errors of metabolism. Also acute confusional migraine, psychiatric causes and arrhythmia.
claims.source_text: Poisoning/toxin Substance abuse or accidental ingestion (eg alcohol, hallucinogens, opiates, lead) … Metabolic and endocrine Hypoglycaemia Diabetic ketoacidosis, renal or hepatic failure, hypo/hypernatremia, hypothermia, inborn error of metabolism … Other Acute confusional migraine, psychiatric, arrhythmia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Attend to ABCDE first, regardless of cause.** If trauma is possible, **immobilise the cervical spine and consult neurosurgery.**
claims.source_text: Regardless of cause of altered conscious state, attend to ABCDE first … If traumatic cause is possible, immobilise cervical spine and consult neurosurgery
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Then identify a cause as quickly as possible.** History: headache, confusion, seizures, focal neurology, abrupt vs gradual course or recurrence, injury, fever, past history including immunisation and development, family history including consanguinity, drug/toxin exposure (quantity, timing) and travel.
claims.source_text: The aim is then to identify a cause as quickly as possible, to guide investigation and treatment … Symptoms: headache, confusion, seizures Focal neurology Time course of symptoms: abrupt vs gradual deterioration, recurrent episodes Injury: mechanism, timing Presence of fever Past and recent medical history including immunisation, seizures, developmental delay Family history including consanguinity Drug and toxin exposure: exposure, quantity, timing Travel history: personal or that of close family contacts
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Signs of raised intracranial pressure:** unilateral or bilateral pupillary dilatation · **GCS drop of more than 2 points** · focal neurology · decorticate or decerebrate posturing · irregular respirations, hypertension and bradycardia (Cushing reflex — **a late sign**).
claims.source_text: Signs of raised intracranial pressure: unilateral or bilateral pupillary dilatation drop of more than 2 points in GCS focal neurological signs abnormal posturing (decorticate, decerebrate) irregular respirations, hypertension and bradycardia (Cushing reflex, a late sign)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examination clues:** rash, petechiae, bruising, needle marks; the smell of alcohol, glue, ketones, petrol or phenol; scalp haematoma, bloody or clear ear/nasal discharge, otitis media, mastoiditis, neck bruising; hepatomegaly or abdominal guarding.
claims.source_text: Skin Rash, petechiae, bruising, birth marks, sweating, needle marks … Smell Alcohol, glue, ketones, petrol, phenol … Head and neck Scalp haematoma, ear/nasal bloody or clear discharge, otitis media, mastoiditis, neck bruising … Hepatomegaly, abdominal guarding, rigidity, or tenderness
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Guided by the differential:** point-of-care glucose; FBE, renal function, glucose, liver function; blood gas, ammonia, cortisol; coagulation; urine toxicology; blood and urine culture.
claims.source_text: Consider the following as guided by your differential diagnoses: … POCT Glucose FBE, renal function, glucose, liver function tests Blood gas, ammonia, cortisol Coagulation profile Urine toxicology … Blood culture, urine culture
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not perform a lumbar puncture in a child with a reduced GCS.** If needed, do it once the child is clinically stable.
claims.source_text: Lumbar puncture: do not perform in a child with a reduced GCS … If required, this can be performed when the child is clinically stable to determine if meningitis, encephalitis, or other neurological condition (such as autoimmune encephalitis etc) are present
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CT or MRI only after initial resuscitation and treatment**, where feasible, for suspected trauma, stroke or raised intracranial pressure.
claims.source_text: CT or MRI (where feasible and only after initial resuscitation and treatment) in suspected trauma, stroke or concerns regarding raised intracranial pressure
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ECG:** a broad QRS suggests critical tricyclic antidepressant toxicity.
claims.source_text: ECG eg broad QRS suggestive of critical tricyclic antidepressant toxicity
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Definitive management follows the working diagnosis** (head injury, trauma, meningitis/encephalitis, sepsis, child abuse, poisoning).
claims.source_text: Definitive management will be guided by the working diagnosis
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspected infection: give antibiotic and antiviral therapy urgently.**
claims.source_text: If suspected infective cause, give antibiotic and antiviral therapy urgently
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat signs of raised intracranial pressure.** For poisoning, 24-hour advice: **Poisons Information Centre 13 11 26.**
claims.source_text: Treat signs of raised intracranial pressure … For 24 hour advice, contact the Poisons Information Centre 13 11 26
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the local paediatric team** for any persistent or unexplained altered conscious state, or any concern for child abuse.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when Any child who presents with persistent or unexplained altered conscious state When there are concerns for child abuse
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider transfer** when the child is at risk of deteriorating and needs management beyond local capability.
claims.source_text: Consider transfer when Child is at risk of deteriorating and requires management beyond the capability of available local services
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider discharge** only when conscious state has returned to normal and there is a clear follow-up plan if required.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when The child’s conscious state has returned to normal There is clear plan for ongoing follow up if required
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Altered conscious state' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Altered_conscious_state/, retrieved 2026-09-23
